Gynecomastia Surgery in Bangalore with Fat-and-Gland Assessment

Gynecomastia is enlargement of male breast tissue from glandular tissue, fat or both, and the treatment plan depends on what is creating the chest fullness. The surgeon assesses chest fat, gland firmness, skin quality, nipple position and medical factors before recommending liposuction, gland excision or a combined approach. Surgery aims to improve chest contour rather than remove the maximum amount of tissue.

What Is GYNECOMASTIA?

Gynecomastia is enlargement of glandular male breast tissue, while pseudogynecomastia refers mainly to excess chest fat; many patients have a mixture of both. Liposuction can reduce diffuse fatty fullness and contour the chest, but firm gland beneath the nipple may require direct excision, often through an incision at the edge of the areola. In more advanced cases with significantly stretched skin, additional skin removal or nipple-areola repositioning may be needed. Surgery does not treat an active hormonal, medication-related or other medical cause, so those contributors should be addressed when relevant before the surgical plan is finalised.

Determine Whether the Fullness Is Fat, Gland or Both

The consultation reviews how long the enlargement has been present, whether it is one-sided or bilateral, tenderness, medicines, supplements, hormone history, weight change and any warning signs needing medical evaluation.

Physical examination distinguishes soft fat from firmer gland tissue and looks at skin excess. In selected cases, blood tests or imaging may be advised before surgery.

OUR PROCESS

OUR GYNECOMASTIA SURGERY PROCESS

The surgeon assesses fat, gland, skin quality, nipple position, asymmetry and overall chest contour, and reviews medicines, supplements, steroid use, symptoms and possible medical causes.

Liposuction, direct gland excision, skin removal or a combined procedure is chosen according to tissue composition and severity.

Includes relevant tests, medicine review, smoking or nicotine use and anaesthesia planning, with additional medical assessment when a hormonal, drug-related or other factor is suspected.

Fat and/or gland tissue is removed according to the agreed design, with attention to smooth transitions. Skin management is added only when the skin cannot retract on its own.

Compression garments, wound care, swelling expectations and activity restrictions are explained. Early walking is encouraged while heavy upper-body training is delayed.

Follow-up reviews incision healing, nipple position, symmetry, scar maturation and whether swelling is masking the developing contour.

Chest training and heavier activity resume gradually once the surgeon confirms healing. Final contour is assessed after swelling settles and the skin adapts.

WHO CAN BENEFIT FROM GYNECOMASTIA SURGERY?

  • Men with Persistent Glandular Chest Enlargement

    Men with persistent firm glandular tissue that does not change meaningfully with weight loss may be candidates for direct excision, once examination confirms it is not simply general chest fat.

  • Men with Mixed Fat and Gland

    Mixed gynecomastia may benefit from combined liposuction and gland removal, which can produce a smoother transition than one technique alone.

  • Men with Localised Chest Fat

    Patients with predominantly fatty fullness and good skin elasticity may be candidates for liposuction-focused contouring, provided dense gland or significant skin excess will not limit the result.

  • Patients with Stable Weight

    A stable weight helps distinguish persistent glandular enlargement from fullness caused by general weight gain, and supports more predictable contour maintenance after surgery.

  • Selected Patients with Skin Excess

    Patients with stretched skin, a low nipple position or more advanced enlargement may need additional skin excision and accept larger scars. A new unilateral lump, nipple discharge, active hormonal disorder or uncontrolled medical condition requires diagnostic evaluation before cosmetic surgery.

Gynaecomastia is planned around anatomy, proportion, safety, recovery and realistic outcome expectations.

Gynecomastia Surgery Cost and Consultation in Bangalore

Cost depends on whether treatment is liposuction, gland excision or both, whether skin removal is needed, and anaesthesia and facility requirements.

  1. 01

    Fat vs Gland Treatment

    Liposuction-only treatment and combined liposuction plus gland excision involve different amounts of surgical work, so the estimate reflects actual tissue composition.

  2. 02

    One-Sided vs Bilateral Surgery

    Unilateral or markedly asymmetrical gynecomastia can require additional planning to balance the two sides.

  3. 03

    Skin Excision

    More advanced grades with significant loose skin may require skin excision and larger scars, with a different recovery pathway.

  4. 04

    Anaesthesia and Follow-Up

    The written estimate should clarify anaesthesia, facility use, compression garments and planned postoperative reviews.

FAQs About Gynaecomastia

Exercise can reduce body fat and build chest muscles, but it does not reliably remove established dense glandular breast tissue.

Clinical examination often distinguishes softer fat from firmer gland. Imaging may be used when the diagnosis is uncertain or another condition needs to be excluded.

Many mixed cases use both, but the exact combination depends on how much fat, gland and skin excess are present.

Removed gland and fat do not usually return in the same way, but weight gain, hormonal changes or certain medicines can alter the chest again.

Walking generally starts early, while heavy upper-body exercise and chest training are reintroduced gradually once healing is secure.

Anaesthesia is used during surgery. Soreness, tightness, bruising and swelling are common during early recovery.

Adolescent gynecomastia can resolve spontaneously. Persistent cases need careful developmental and medical assessment before elective surgery is considered.
